_meta.doc: RoD v2.8 OVERNIGHT FLYWHEEL — fully-resolved run config (the single machine-readable source of truth for this run)
_meta.status: MEASUREMENT ONLY — exploratory overnight line. NO promotion, PRODUCTION.yaml UNCHANGED, champion (flywheel2_champion_iter8) UNCHANGED, v2.7 frozen, v2.8 opt-in.
_meta.question: Does the v2.8 RoD continuation gain (RoD_iter_01 beat its parent +53.4) COMPOUND across a multi-iteration latest-chain flywheel, or does it saturate like the v2.7 substrate did?
_meta.not_a: NOT a promotion-grade run; cheap screens are catastrophe detectors, not strength verdicts. Binding evals run TOMORROW on selected checkpoints.

lineage.policy: latest-chain — warm-from the PREVIOUS iter every time (RoD_iter_01 -> RoD_iter_02 -> RoD_iter_03 -> ...). ALL checkpoints retained for after-the-fact keep-best tomorrow.
lineage.catastrophe_rule: On a COLLAPSE screen (entropy < 0.5*baseline, NaN loss, val_pol blow-up, or smoke wr-vs-parent < 0.25) the chain STOPS cleanly at the last-sane checkpoint; all artifacts preserved.

frozen_recipe._comment: EVERY axis below is IDENTICAL to the recipe that produced RoD_iter_01 (the user's hard constraint). The ONLY knob set to a different-but-validated value is games/iter (see deviations).
frozen_recipe.leaf_env_warning: do NOT use CARCASSONNE_V28_MEEPLE_K (object path, 2.26x slower, recovery-scaled, hurt ~75 elo). Legacy field keeps the FLAT/Cython fast path (_v28_active stays False).

games_per_iter.rationale: games/iter is NOT in the user's frozen-recipe list (batch/LR/epochs/arch/c_puct/residual/sims). 400 is the VALIDATED attempt-2 flywheel cadence (the residual flywheel ran 400 games/iter x 8 iters -> champion iter8, +67 elo compounding). The continuation's 1000 was a ONE-SHOT probe boost, not the flywheel cadence. 400 keeps every frozen axis identical while making 10+ iters feasible overnight. In a warm-from CHAIN the under-training concern (cf. batch-512) does NOT apply: each iter fine-tunes the already-converged policy on fresh data; the chain accumulates steps across iters.
games_per_iter.reversible: set GAMES=1000 to run the exact continuation data volume (then ~4-5 iters fit overnight instead of ~9-10).

cluster.gen: 2-box work-stealing via carc-orch SHM orchestrator (USE_ORCH=1), --shared-claim claim files in the shared iterN_data dir; both boxes drain ONE game pool.
cluster.train: LOCAL only (5900XT). Training is GPU-latency-bound; the laptop trains ~10% slower (memory reference_training_latency_bound).
cluster.smoke: LOCAL only, two carc-orch contexts (one per checkpoint).

workers_orch._note: user directive was 'w 48 and 26'. Local 48 = tuned EVAL_W (44dbc42), verified RAM-safe on the 32GB box. Laptop 26 is the EVAL ceiling but GEN workers are heavier: the W26 gen PRE-FLIGHT (2026-06-23) wedged the laptop at ~131MB free and OOM-stalled sshd -> dropped to W8 = the documented gen-safe + throughput-optimal value (gen_flywheel.sh:49 sweep). Both boxes RAM-monitored during the re-validated pre-flight.

cluster.code_sync: git bundle carc_stage-b-wiring.bundle on the share; laptop git-resets to it (gen code == stage-b-wiring, unchanged on this branch). If laptop sync fails -> auto local-only.

loop_control.self_play_seed_note: per-iter band = 620000000 + iter*100000, all < 1e9 (self-play namespace), disjoint from the continuation's 600010000.
loop_control.smoke_seed_note: >= 1e9 eval floor; disjoint from spent eval bands (1.7e9 sealed, 1.906/1.907e9 battery, 1.922/1.923e9 b512).
loop_control.smoke_note: two-context net-vs-net is GPU-latency-bound + startup-dominated (~80s dual TorchScript export/boot). Measured n=10@OW32 = 194s -> n=16 ~= 4 min/iter (~40 min over 10 iters). CATASTROPHE DETECTOR ONLY (wr<0.25 vs prev = collapse); n far too small for strength.
loop_control.stall_heal: gen no-progress for 15 polls x 60s -> kill pools+orch on both boxes, clean stranded claims, relaunch; abort after 8 heals.

deferred_to_tomorrow._comment: NOT run overnight (cost discipline — the user's 'Full eval deferral').

deferred_to_tomorrow.selection: latest checkpoint + best cheap/root-diagnostic checkpoint + maybe every 2nd if unclear (after-the-fact keep-best).
